newsitem.title: USA: Schnuck Markets to pay $3 million for violation.
newsitem.headline: Schnuck Markets to pay $3 million for violation.

text.p: Schnuck Markets Inc. of St. Louis, Mo., will pay a $3 million civil penalty for permitting two dozen stores to go downhill before turning them over to competitors under a promise to the government.
The settlement is one of the largest ever obtained for violating an order of the Federal Trade Commission, the FTC said Wednesday.
In 1995, the Federal Trade commission permitted Schnucks to acquire supermarkets owned by National Holdings Inc. In return, Schnuck' agreed to divest 24 specific groceries.

Schnuck sold off the stores, but not before it got them unlisted telephone numbers, shut down their bakeries, delis, seafood, flower and video departments, copied their pharmacy records and permitted the stores to run out of stock, the FTC said.
At the same time, it gave customers coupons claiming the stores would close and directing them to other Schnuck stores, the FTC said.
Not surprisingly, patronage dropped at those stores -- undermining the intent of the 1995 consent decree to preserve competition by requiring the divestiture, the FTC said.
"We were prepared to prove in court that Schnuck's allowed these stores to deteriorate badly before they were sold," said William Baer, director of the FTC Bureau of Competition.
